title: Digital Biomarkers for Hormone-Mediated Insulin Resistance and Context-Aware Diabetes Management (HORMONITOR)
summary: In people with type 1 diabetes, the amount of insulin needed can vary from day to day. Sleep, stress, physical activity, acute illness, and hormonal changes, including changes across the menstrual cycle, may contribute to this variability. HORMONITOR investigates how these everyday factors are related to glucose patterns and insulin action. The study will include 50 adults who already use a community-developed open-source system that automatically adjusts insulin delivery. For six months, data from their glucose sensor, insulin pump, and a smartwatch or ring will be combined. Participants also complete regular questionnaires about sleep, stress, quality of life, diabetes-related burden, and hormone-related symptoms. The study does not change treatment or device settings. Participation is mainly digital and location-independent. The aim is to identify individual patterns that may improve understanding of changes in insulin action and glucose levels.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Age 18 years or older at the time of consent
- Written informed consent before any study-specific procedures
- Diagnosis of type 1 diabetes
- Current use for at least one month of a smartphone-based open-source automated insulin delivery system from the OpenAPS oref family, such as AndroidAPS or Trio
- Ability and willingness to share AID, glucose sensor, wearable, and contextual data through the study application and SENSOR-HUB infrastructure
- Willingness to wear a compatible smartwatch or ring throughout the study period, either participant-owned or provided by the study team
- Sufficient proficiency in a study language to complete the validated questionnaires: English, German, Spanish, Dutch, or Mandarin Chinese
Exclusion criteria:
- Known allergy or intolerance to materials used in wearable devices
- Severe cognitive impairment, insufficiently managed psychiatric illness, or another medical condition likely to prevent reliable participation or continuous data contribution
- Current participation in another interventional clinical trial that could interfere with data collection or interpretation
- Pregnancy or planned pregnancy during the study period
- Inability to operate a smartphone or wearable reliably, even with onboarding support
